limitations: Scoring reflects a predeclared 10-category rubric applied consistently within this shard; category weightings are equal (10 points each) and were fixed before evidence collection.

Some sub-scores (message queues, CI/CD, IoT) rely on general ecosystem knowledge of widely known libraries (kafkajs, amqplib, Octokit, kubernetes-client-node, MQTT.js) that were not individually re-verified via search in this pass due to the 5-search budget for this work unit; these are well-established, uncontroversial facts about the npm/TypeScript ecosystem.

This worker is a single-language shard (TypeScript only) per the assigned Task Packet; only the TypeScript key is populated for both metrics, consistent with runner merge expectations for disjoint-language shards.
evidence.methodology_note: Metrics scored against a single frozen 10-category rubric each (10 points per category, sum=0-100), applied identically to all 10 languages across shards. Category selection is predeclared and independent of any language's benchmark performance. Evidence collected via official documentation, project repositories, and vendor pages for TypeScript only in this shard; other language shards apply the same category list and point scheme.

metric.external_integration_coverage.scoring_rule: 10 points per domain if official or de-facto standard, actively maintained integration libraries exist with reliable TypeScript typings; partial credit for community-only or partial typing coverage.

ai_ml_platforms.citation: <cite index="40-1">This library provides convenient access to the OpenAI REST API from TypeScript or JavaScript.</cite>
ai_ml_platforms.justification: OpenAI's official Node/TypeScript SDK, along with TensorFlow.js and Hugging Face's JS SDKs, provide first-class TypeScript-typed access to major AI platforms.

api_protocols.justification: REST, GraphQL (Apollo, urql), and gRPC (@grpc/grpc-js with generated TS types) are all well supported with mature, actively maintained TypeScript tooling.

auth_identity.justification: OAuth2/OIDC libraries (Passport, next-auth, Auth0's official SDK) provide typed integration for the Node/TypeScript ecosystem.

cicd_devops.justification: GitHub's official Octokit client and the Kubernetes JavaScript client are TypeScript-typed, covering common CI/CD and orchestration automation needs.

cloud_providers.citation: <cite index="5-1,5-2">The AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 is written in TypeScript. Full type definitions are included in every package, giving you type hints, autocompletion, and compile-time safety</cite>
cloud_providers.justification: AWS SDK for JavaScript v3 is itself written in TypeScript with first-class type definitions shipped in every package; comparable official TS-typed SDKs exist for Azure and GCP.

databases.justification: Mature, widely used TypeScript-first ORMs and drivers (Prisma, TypeORM, Mongoose, node-postgres) cover both relational and NoSQL databases.

iot_hardware.justification: MQTT.js and related IoT protocol libraries provide working TypeScript integration, though typings and platform reach are more limited than for web/cloud-centric domains.

message_queues.justification: Kafka, RabbitMQ, and cloud queue clients (kafkajs, amqplib, AWS SQS via the TS-authored AWS SDK) provide typed integration, though typings are sometimes community-maintained rather than official.

observability.justification: OpenTelemetry's JavaScript SDK plus vendor SDKs (Sentry, Datadog) provide TypeScript-typed instrumentation for tracing, metrics, and error monitoring.

payments_commerce.justification: Stripe's official Node.js SDK ships full TypeScript type definitions, and PayPal and other payment providers offer comparable typed SDKs.

metric.implemented_platform_coverage.scoring_rule: 10 points per category if mainstream, actively maintained tooling exists that lets the language target that platform as a first-class or well-supported use case; partial credit (4-6) for niche/limited/indirect support; 0 for no meaningful support. Sum across 10 categories = 0-100 raw score.

cloud_native_containers.citation: <cite index="1-1">The AWS SDK for JavaScript is written in TypeScript.</cite>
cloud_native_containers.justification: Node.js/TypeScript services are widely containerized and TypeScript-based clients exist for Kubernetes and cloud infrastructure APIs (e.g., the AWS SDK for JavaScript, written in TypeScript, used broadly in containerized cloud workloads).

desktop.citation: <cite index="27-1">A modern, lightweight starter template for building cross-platform desktop applications with Tauri, React, TypeScript, and shadcn/ui</cite>
desktop.justification: Electron and Tauri both provide mature, actively maintained TypeScript project templates for cross-platform desktop apps.

embedded_iot.citation: <cite index="36-8">Despite its web nature, WebAssembly can also run in non-web modes, such as servers, IoT devices, Mobile/Desktop applications, taking into account some web features will not be available.</cite>
embedded_iot.justification: JavaScript/TypeScript can run on some microcontroller-class devices via engines like Espruino or through Node-based IoT frameworks (Johnny-Five), but this is a niche use case relative to C/C++/Rust in embedded contexts, and typing support there is limited.

game_development.justification: TypeScript is used with web-oriented game engines/libraries (Phaser, Babylon.js, Excalibur.js) but has no mainstream presence in native/console AAA engines, unlike C++.

mobile.citation: <cite index="8-11">The modular AWS SDK for JavaScript officially supports Node.js, browser and React Native environments.</cite>
mobile.justification: React Native and related frameworks ship official TypeScript templates and the modular AWS SDK explicitly lists React Native as an officially supported platform alongside Node.js and browsers.

server_backend.citation: <cite index="11-1,11-2,11-3,11-4">TypeScript >= 4.9 is supported ... Node.js 20 LTS or later (non-EOL) versions. Deno v1.28.0 or higher. Bun 1.0 or later.</cite>
server_backend.justification: Node.js, Deno, and Bun all provide first-class TypeScript execution/build support for backend services.

serverless_edge.citation: <cite index="17-1,17-2">TypeScript is a first-class language on Cloudflare Workers. All APIs provided in Workers are fully typed, and type definitions are generated directly from workerd</cite>
serverless_edge.justification: Cloudflare Workers, a major edge/serverless platform, treats TypeScript as a first-class language with runtime-generated type definitions; AWS Lambda's Node.js runtime bundles the TS-authored SDK by default.

systems_level.justification: TypeScript, running atop a JS engine, is not used for OS kernels, drivers, or other systems-level programming; no mainstream toolchain targets this domain.

web_browser.citation: <cite index="7-8,7-9,7-10">Angular is written in TypeScript since version 2.0, and it recommends TypeScript as a primary language for application development. Vue.js is another popular JavaScript frontend framework, and Vue 3 is written in TypeScript. The Create React App tool of React also added TypeScript support in v2.1.0.</cite>
web_browser.justification: TypeScript is transpiled to JavaScript and is the dominant typed language for browser frontend frameworks (Angular, Vue 3, React tooling).

webassembly.citation: <cite index="31-1,31-14">AssemblyScript defines a subset of TypeScript that it compiles to WebAssembly ... Every AssemblyScript program is valid TypeScript syntactically, but not necessarily semantically.</cite>
webassembly.justification: TypeScript itself is not compiled directly to WebAssembly by tsc; reaching Wasm requires AssemblyScript, a related but distinct strict subset/variant of TypeScript with its own compiler and semantic limitations, so support is indirect rather than native to the TypeScript toolchain.
